name: Dylan Scott
who: American Elite 15 racer, the 2026 HYROX World Champion after a chaotic wall-ball finish in Stockholm.
why: The reigning world champion right now — his 2025 bronze-to-2026 gold arc is the story of the season.
takeaway: Drill your finishing station so a close race doesn't slip away late.

name: Tim Wenisch
who: German Elite 15 racer, 2025 HYROX World Champion and 2026 Elite Doubles World Champion with Alexander Roncevic.
why: Defending champion energy carried into a new title — still on every 2026 podium that matters.
takeaway: Race both singles and doubles in the same season to build all-around fitness.

name: Hunter McIntyre
who: American Elite 15 racer, three-time HYROX World Champion (2020, 2022, 2023) and former OCR/CrossFit Games competitor.
why: The sport's biggest crossover name — still winning Pro titles in 2026 and the athlete non-Hyrox fans have actually heard of.
reach: IG follower count not independently verified this session (approx, unverified 2026)
takeaway: Bring skills from other disciplines, like OCR or CrossFit, into training instead of specializing narrow.

name: Alexander Roncevic
who: Austrian Elite 15 racer, Men's Pro world record holder (51:59, Warsaw) and 2024 HYROX World Champion.
why: The fastest man ever to race HYROX — took the 2026 doubles title even after a rough singles final.

name: Louis Osselaer
who: Belgian Elite 15 racer who went from age-group world champion to 2026 HYROX World Championships silver medalist.
why: This season's breakout — the sled-pull specialist nobody was talking about until he nearly won Stockholm.
takeaway: Turn a weak station into a specialty — dedicated focus on one weakness can carry you to a podium.

name: James Kelly
who: Australia's fastest HYROX athlete, Elite 15 racer, 4th at the 2025 World Championships and part of Australia's winning 2026 relay team.
why: One of the most consistent vloggers in the sport — weekly training breakdowns make him a go-to for how to actually train.
takeaway: Document your own training weekly — the habit of review builds skill faster than random workouts.

name: Jake Dearden
who: British Elite 15 racer, former HYROX Men's Doubles World Champion and the sport's biggest social following.
why: By far the largest reach in HYROX and a genuine crossover figure — podcasts, brand deals, and stunt charity races.
takeaway: Keep racing yourself even after you start coaching — it keeps your advice honest.

name: Rich Ryan
who: American Elite 15 racer and coach, a regular top-15 singles finisher who took Elite Doubles bronze in 2026 with Pelayo Menendez.
why: Steady Elite 15 mainstay whose coaching content translates his own race data into usable advice.
takeaway: Work on your running strategy inside the race itself, not just station strength.

name: Pelayo Menendez
who: Spanish Elite 15 racer and founder of PELE Performance, back on the 2026 World Championships doubles podium a year after a ruptured Achilles.
why: The leading Spanish-language voice in the sport — constant Instagram lives, podcasts, and Facebook-group coaching.
takeaway: Rehab a serious injury with patience and return to racing rather than rushing back.

name: Tomas Tvrdik
who: Czech soldier and Elite 15 racer, EMEA champion in 2026 with a sub-55-minute personal best at age 40.
why: No man over 40 has gone faster — a genuine outlier chasing a world title on almost no training volume.
takeaway: Chase a fast pace even on low training volume by prioritizing quality sessions over total hours.

name: Cole Learn
who: Canadian Elite 15 racer, 2026 HYROX Americas Champion and Chicago Pro winner (54:36) with a public addiction-recovery story.
why: Fast-rising racer whose personal story pulls readers who have never heard of HYROX before.
takeaway: Use consistent race training itself as a structured recovery tool.

name: Hidde Weersma
who: Dutch Elite 15 racer and coach who broke the Men's Pro world record (52:42) at the 2026 EMEA Championships in London.
why: First man under 53 minutes and the mind behind LO:HYROX, a data-driven training program other Elite 15 racers use.
takeaway: Use data-driven pacing plans for each station instead of racing on feel alone.

name: Sebastian Ifversen
who: Danish Elite 15 racer with dozens of races across six seasons and consistent top-10 major finishes.
why: A dependable Elite 15 name for readers tracking the full field, not just the podium.
takeaway: Rack up race experience across many seasons — consistent finishes come from repeated starts, not one big prep.

name: Charlie Botterill
who: English Elite 15 racer and former pro cyclist, part of the second-fastest Men's Pro Doubles time ever run (48:05, Barcelona 2026).
why: Quit his job to go all-in on HYROX in 2026 — a fast-rising name with a genuinely different backstory.
takeaway: Go all-in on training for a season if you're serious about a breakthrough result.

name: Graham Halliday
who: Scottish Elite 15 racer, widely regarded as the UK's fastest HYROX athlete, 10th at the 2025 World Championships.
why: Full-time coach and gym owner whose podcast and YouTube channel teach the sport from race-day intensity down to basics.
takeaway: Learn the sport from both ends — race-day intensity and the basics — not just one.

name: Tobias Lautwein
who: German HYROX World Champion (2021) and European Champion (2022), a former world-record holder now racing at Pro rather than Elite 15 level.
why: One of the sport's earliest champions — still racing and still a name podcasts want, though he dropped out of the Elite 15 for 2025-26.
takeaway: Keep racing at whatever level fits your current life, even after stepping down from the top tier.

name: Dexter Buchanan
who: New Zealand racer, one of seven new qualifiers to the 2026 HYROX Elite 15 men's field.
why: Worth watching as a first-season Elite 15 name from a country new to the sport's top tier.
takeaway: Qualify for the top tier before worrying about results there — making the field is the first goal.

name: Sean Noble
who: Irish racer, one of seven new qualifiers to the 2026 HYROX Elite 15 men's field.
why: A first-season Elite 15 name to watch as Ireland's presence in the sport's top tier grows.
takeaway: Treat your first Elite 15 season as building experience, not chasing an immediate podium.

name: Luke Greer
who: English racer, one of seven new qualifiers to the 2026 HYROX Elite 15 men's field.
why: New to the Elite 15 in 2026 and part of a deep British contingent at the top of the sport.
takeaway: Push into a deep national field on purpose — tougher training partners at home raise your ceiling.
